summary.en: Venezuelan forces are reported to have bombed an ELN camp near the Colombia border, killing at least 19, while a drone strike allegedly destroyed an ELN drug depot in the same area, causing at least 20 deaths. Opposition leader María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela and called for elections, delivering her first address since her return. President Trump has referenced the Maduro capture operation while discussing Cuba and suggested possible U.S. action against Cuba, and he claimed Venezuelan oil revenues far exceed Iran war costs. Chevron is expanding operations in Venezuela as Exxon urges caution. There were 2 battle-related deaths in 2007, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Venezuelanske styrker skal ha bombet en ELN-leir nær grensen mot Colombia, og drept minst 19 personer, mens et droneangrep angivelig ødela et ELN-drogdepot i samme område, og forårsaket minst 20 dødsfall. Opposisjonslederen María Corina Machado kom tilbake til Venezuela og oppfordret til valg, og holdt sin første tale siden hun kom tilbake. President Trump har referert til operasjonen for å fange Maduro mens han snakket om Cuba og antydet mulig amerikansk handling mot Cuba, og han hevdet at inntektene fra venezuelansk olje langt overgår Irans krigskostnader. Chevron utvider virksomheten i Venezuela mens Exxon oppfordrer til forsiktighet. Det var 2 dødsfall i kamp i 2007, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Crisis in Venezuela
background.extract: An ongoing socioeconomic and political crisis began in Venezuela during the presidencies of Hugo Chávez, Nicolás Maduro and Delcy Rodríguez. It has been marked by hyperinflation, starvation, disease, crime, and mortality rates, resulting in massive emigration. Food shortages and hyperinflation have ended, but inflation remains high. It is the worst economic crisis in Venezuela's history and considered by some sources as more severe than the Great Depression in the United States, the 1985–1994 Brazilian economic crisis, or the 2008–2009 hyperinflation in Zimbabwe. In 2019, the Institute of International Finance called it the single largest economic collapse outside of war in 45 years. Writers have compared aspects, such as unemployment and GDP contraction, to Bosnia and Herzegovina after the 1992–95 Bosnian War, and those in Russia, Cuba and Albania following the Revolutions of 1989.
